airplane: Airplanes are distinct aerial vehicles characterized by their fixed-wing structure, fuselage, and tail fins, appearing as discrete objects often clustered on paved aprons or along taxiways. Unlike airports, which are expansive transportation hubs with long runways and terminals, airplanes are individual aircraft objects; compared to runways, which are long, uniform gray strips, airplanes have specific structural geometries; and unlike parking lots, which contain clustered rectangular cars, airplanes are larger with distinct wings.
airport: Airports are large aviation hubs characterized by long, wide gray runways with bright white markings, taxiways, and large terminal buildings. Unlike runways, which are just the landing strips, airports include the entire complex of buildings and infrastructure; compared to industrial areas, airports focus on aviation rather than manufacturing buildings; and unlike parking lots, which contain rows of cars, airports have large aprons with passenger boarding bridges.
baseball_diamond: A baseball diamond is defined by its distinctive fan-shaped layout, featuring a brown or tan dirt infield, white base paths, and a green outfield. Unlike basketball courts, which are rectangular with hard surfaces, baseball diamonds have a curved outfield boundary; compared to ground track fields, which have oval running tracks, baseball diamonds have a specific diamond and arc pattern; and unlike tennis courts, which are small rectangles, baseball diamonds are larger with a dirt infield.
basketball_court: A basketball court is a rectangular area characterized by hard surfaces and distinct white line markings for boundaries, hoops, and free-throw lines. Unlike tennis courts, which are divided by a net, basketball courts have specific painted lines and hoops; compared to ground track fields, which are large and oval, basketball courts are smaller and rectangular; and unlike parking lots, which are filled with cars, basketball courts are empty recreational surfaces.
beach: Beach areas are coastal strips of bright tan or white sand separating the ocean from inland terrain, often with adjacent developments. Unlike harbors, which are water-land interfaces with docks and ships, beaches are natural sandy shores; compared to islands, which are surrounded by water, beaches are coastal margins of larger landmasses; and unlike wetlands, which are vegetated marshes, beaches are dry sandy strips.
bridge: Bridges are linear structures spanning water bodies or valleys, appearing as straight or curved paved roads connecting separate landmasses. Unlike railways, which are ground-level tracks, bridges are elevated structures spanning gaps; compared to rivers, which are flowing water, bridges are paved transit structures; and unlike intersections, which are ground-level road junctions, bridges are elevated crossings.
chaparral: Chaparral is characterized by a continuous, rough, and mottled texture of dense, low-growing woody vegetation in natural terrain, typically appearing in muted green or brown tones. Unlike forests, which have tall tree canopies, chaparral consists of low shrubs; compared to meadows, which are smooth grass, chaparral is rough and woody; and unlike deserts, which are barren sand, chaparral has dense low vegetation.
church: Churches are identified by their distinct religious architecture, often featuring sharp spires, crosses, or pitched roofs, and usually stand isolated in neighborhoods. Unlike palaces, which are large and sprawling, churches are isolated structures with religious symbols; compared to commercial areas, which are retail zones, churches are places of worship; and unlike railway stations, which are transit hubs, churches have distinct vertical features.
circular_farmland: Circular farmland is characterized by distinct circular patterns of irrigated crops, often showing green vegetation within tan or brown field boundaries. Unlike rectangular farmland, which is divided by straight grid lines, circular farmland has pivot irrigation patterns; compared to meadows, which are natural grass, circular farmland has organized agricultural circles; and unlike forests, which are dense trees, circular farmland is open land with crops.
cloud: Clouds appear as soft, diffuse, white or gray masses overlaying the landscape, often casting distinct shadows on the ground beneath them. Unlike snowbergs, which are solid and fixed to the terrain, clouds are atmospheric and fluffy; compared to islands, which are surrounded by water, clouds float above land or sea; and unlike deserts, which are ground-based sand, clouds are atmospheric vapor.
commercial_area: Commercial areas are filled with large, rectangular buildings with flat roofs, often surrounded by parking lots, located along main roads. Unlike industrial areas, which have large factories, commercial areas have retail buildings; compared to residential areas, which have housing units, commercial areas have larger commercial footprints; and unlike parking lots, which are flat surfaces, commercial areas have large vertical structures.
dense_residential: Dense residential areas consist of tightly packed small buildings with uniform, repetitive roof patterns, creating a high-density spatial layout with minimal vegetation. Unlike medium residential areas, which have more space between buildings, dense residential areas have smaller footprints and tighter spacing; compared to sparse residential areas, dense residential areas have much higher density; and unlike industrial areas, which are factories, dense residential areas are housing.
desert: Deserts are vast, continuous expanses of flat terrain covered with sand, exhibiting uniform light tan or yellow colors. Unlike beaches, which are coastal strips, deserts are inland expanses; compared to mountains, which are rugged and elevated, deserts are flat; and unlike forests, which are dense trees, deserts lack vegetation.
forest: Forest areas are identified by a continuous, dense canopy of trees with a rough, mottled texture and dark green tones, often casting collective shadows. Unlike chaparral, which is low shrubs, forests have tall tree canopies; compared to meadows, which are short grass, forests have dense trees; and unlike mountains, which have rocky peaks, forests are tree-covered.
freeway: Freeways are wide, multi-lane linear transportation networks with smooth gray surfaces, often intersecting or crossing overpasses. Unlike railways, which are ground-level tracks, freeways are wide paved roads for vehicles; compared to bridges, which span water, freeways are continuous land routes; and unlike parking lots, which are stationary vehicle storage, freeways are continuous transit lines.
golf_course: Golf courses are large expanses of manicured green turf with distinct linear boundaries and water hazards, featuring patterns of fairways and putting greens. Unlike parks, which are general recreation, golf courses have specific fairway patterns; compared to forests, which are dense trees, golf courses are open grass with isolated trees; and unlike meadows, which are natural grass, golf courses are manicured turf.
ground_track_field: Ground track fields are large, oval-shaped sporting areas defined by concentric colored lanes and a central green or dirt infield. Unlike basketball courts, which are rectangular, track fields are oval with concentric lanes; compared to baseball diamonds, which have a diamond pattern, track fields have a running track surrounding a central field; and unlike parking lots, which store cars, track fields are sports surfaces.
harbor: Harbors are coastal water-land interfaces characterized by clustered ships, cranes, and linear docks, serving as hubs for maritime shipping. Unlike airports, which have runways and planes, harbors have docks and ships; compared to bridges, which span water, harbors are docking areas for ships; and unlike industrial areas, which have factories, harbors focus on maritime logistics.
industrial_area: Industrial areas contain large, rectangular factory buildings with metallic roofs, often accompanied by storage tanks or loading docks. Unlike commercial areas, which are retail zones, industrial areas have massive manufacturing buildings; compared to airports, which have runways, industrial areas lack aviation infrastructure; and unlike residential areas, which are housing, industrial areas are manufacturing zones.
intersection: An intersection is a junction where two or more roads cross, forming a distinct cross, T-shape, or complex multi-lane interchange pattern. Unlike overpasses, which are elevated crossings, intersections are at-grade road junctions; compared to freeways, which are continuous linear routes, intersections are nodes; and unlike parking lots, which are stationary storage, intersections are traffic flow junctions.
island: Islands are landmasses completely surrounded by water, appearing in various shapes and sizes with coastlines. Unlike beaches, which are coastal margins, islands are surrounded by water on all sides; compared to lakes, which are water surrounded by land, islands are land surrounded by water; and unlike bridges, which connect landmasses, islands are isolated landforms.
lake: Lakes are large, static bodies of water enclosed by land, appearing as dark blue or black shapes with irregular or smooth shorelines. Unlike rivers, which are flowing water, lakes are static; compared to islands, which are land surrounded by water, lakes are water surrounded by land; and unlike wetlands, which are vegetated, lakes are open water bodies.
meadow: Meadows are expanses of open, natural grassy terrain with a smooth texture and light green color, lacking tree cover. Unlike circular farmland, which has organized patterns, meadows are natural grass; compared to forests, which are dense trees, meadows are open grass; and unlike golf courses, which are manicured, meadows are natural unmanicured terrain.
medium_residential: Medium residential areas display a mix of single-family homes with moderate spacing, showing a balance between built structures and surrounding greenery or lawns. Unlike dense residential areas, which are tightly packed, medium residential areas have larger yards; compared to sparse residential areas, medium residential areas have higher density; and unlike commercial areas, which have retail buildings, medium residential areas are housing.
mobile_home_park: Mobile home parks are characterized by densely arranged, small, rectangular housing units with uniform, flat, and light-colored roofs, often aligned in rows. Unlike dense residential areas, which have more complex roofs, mobile home parks have uniform flat roofs; compared to parking lots, which are flat surfaces, mobile home parks are small housing units; and unlike industrial areas, which are large factories, mobile home parks are small residential units.
mountain: Mountainous regions are characterized by rugged, elevated topography with steep slopes, rocky peaks, and intricate shadow patterns caused by the terrain. Unlike forests, which are tree-covered, mountains show exposed rock; compared to deserts, which are flat sand, mountains have elevation changes; and unlike beaches, which are coastal, mountains are inland elevated landforms.
overpass: Overpasses are elevated road structures that cross over other roads or terrain, appearing as distinct curved or linear bridge segments separated from the ground surface. Unlike intersections, which are at-grade crossings, overpasses are grade-separated; compared to freeways, which are continuous routes, overpasses are crossing structures; and unlike bridges, which cross water, overpasses cross roads or land.
palace: Palaces are large, sprawling structures with complex, ornate architecture, often featuring courtyards, multiple wings, and prominent vertical structures. Unlike churches, which are isolated religious buildings, palaces are large residential compounds; compared to commercial areas, which are retail zones, palaces are large residential or governmental structures; and unlike railway stations, which are transit hubs, palaces are monumental buildings.
parking_lot: Parking lots are large, flat, paved rectangular areas with visible grid-like rows of parked vehicles, often adjacent to buildings or commercial zones. Unlike mobile home parks, which are small housing units, parking lots contain transient vehicles; compared to commercial areas, which have large buildings, parking lots are flat surfaces; and unlike airports, which have runways, parking lots are vehicle storage areas.
railway: Railways are linear ground-level transportation networks consisting of parallel tracks and occasionally passing trains, often cutting through natural or urban terrain. Unlike freeways, which are paved roads for vehicles, railways have tracks; compared to bridges, which are elevated, railways are ground-level; and unlike airports, which have runways, railways have narrow parallel tracks.
railway_station: Railway stations are transit hubs characterized by linear clusters of train cars, long parallel platforms, and station buildings. Unlike airports, which have planes and runways, railway stations have trains and tracks; compared to industrial areas, which are manufacturing zones, railway stations are passenger transit hubs; and unlike commercial areas, which are retail zones, railway stations focus on train logistics.
rectangular_farmland: Rectangular farmland consists of regular geometric plots of cultivated land with varying textures and colors, showing distinct crop rows or soil boundaries. Unlike circular farmland, which has pivot irrigation, rectangular farmland has straight grid boundaries; compared to meadows, which are natural grass, rectangular farmland has organized agricultural plots; and unlike forests, which are dense trees, rectangular farmland is open land with crops.
river: Rivers are natural, flowing water bodies with sinuous, irregular curves that adapt to the topography, often surrounded by riparian vegetation. Unlike bridges, which are paved structures, rivers are water bodies; compared to lakes, which are static, rivers are flowing; and unlike wetlands, which are vegetated, rivers are open flowing water.
roundabout: Roundabouts are circular road junctions where traffic flows continuously around a central island, often featuring landscaped or decorative centers. Unlike intersections, which are cross or T-shaped junctions, roundabouts have circular layouts; compared to circular farmland, which is agricultural, roundabouts are paved traffic nodes; and unlike baseball diamonds, which are sports fields, roundabouts are traffic control structures.
runway: Runways are long, wide, and straight paved surfaces with distinct white or yellow edge and centerline markings, designed for aircraft operations. Unlike freeways, which have multiple lanes, runways are single wide strips; compared to airports, which include terminals, runways are just the landing strips; and unlike railways, which have tracks, runways are solid paved surfaces.
sea_ice: Sea ice appears as floating, fragmented white masses on the ocean surface, often with distinct edges and varying concentrations of ice floes. Unlike islands, which are solid land, sea ice is frozen water; compared to snowbergs, which are elevated ice mountains, sea ice is flat and floating; and unlike lakes, which are surrounded by land, sea ice is on the ocean.
ship: Ships are discrete watercraft of various sizes, often appearing as elongated dark or white objects floating in water, sometimes clustered in harbors. Unlike airplanes, which are in the air or on runways, ships are on water; compared to harbors, which are docking areas, ships are the vessels themselves; and unlike bridges, which are stationary, ships are mobile objects.
snowberg: Snowbergs are elevated, white or light-gray masses of snow and ice, often found on mountains or in polar regions, with distinct shadow patterns. Unlike mountains, which have exposed rock, snowbergs are covered in snow; compared to sea ice, which is flat floating ice, snowbergs are elevated; and unlike deserts, which are sand, snowbergs are snow and ice.
sparse_residential: Sparse residential areas are characterized by widely spaced individual houses surrounded by large expanses of natural or undeveloped land, showing very low housing density. Unlike dense residential areas, which are tightly packed, sparse residential areas have large distances between buildings; compared to medium residential areas, sparse residential areas have lower density; and unlike commercial areas, which have retail buildings, sparse residential areas are housing.
stadium: Stadiums are large, enclosed structures featuring a massive central playing field surrounded by tiered seating, often with a distinctive oval or circular footprint. Unlike playgrounds, which are small open areas, stadiums are massive enclosed structures; compared to palaces, which are residential, stadiums are sports venues; and unlike industrial areas, which are factories, stadiums are large sports complexes.
storage_tank: Storage tanks are circular, cylindrical structures with smooth surfaces and distinct shadows, often grouped closely together in industrial zones. Unlike parking lots, which are flat surfaces with cars, storage tanks are elevated 3D structures; compared to buildings, which are rectangular, storage tanks are circular; and unlike harbors, which have ships, storage tanks are stationary industrial structures.
tennis_court: Tennis courts are rectangular, smooth green or blue surfaces with distinct white boundary lines and net markers, usually arranged in groups within recreational areas. Unlike basketball courts, which have hoops, tennis courts have nets; compared to ground track fields, which are oval, tennis courts are small rectangles; and unlike parking lots, which have cars, tennis courts are empty recreational surfaces.
terrace: Terraces are step-like structures carved into sloping terrain, creating flat agricultural plots on hillsides, often showing linear or parallel patterns. Unlike circular farmland, which is flat, terraces are carved into slopes; compared to forests, which are trees, terraces are agricultural plots; and unlike mountains, which are rugged, terraces are modified agricultural terrain.
thermal_power_station: Thermal power stations are industrial complexes featuring large buildings, cooling towers, and sometimes smokestacks, often located near water bodies or coal storage. Unlike industrial areas, which are general factories, thermal power stations have distinct cooling towers; compared to airports, which have runways, thermal power stations have smokestacks and towers; and unlike railway stations, which are transit hubs, thermal power stations are power generation facilities.
wetland: Wetlands are transitional areas between land and water, characterized by a mix of shallow water, marshes, and dense riparian vegetation, often showing mottled textures. Unlike lakes, which are open water, wetlands are vegetated; compared to rivers, which are flowing, wetlands are static or slow-moving; and unlike forests, which are dry land trees, wetlands are water-saturated vegetation.
